Reviewed all six proof steps, the full Cartier/Picard proof, full curve-additivity proof, exact twisting/projection interfaces, global-generation and ampleness hypotheses, and the owning page and contract. Expanding the four Euler terms gives the displayed shift defect; the quadratic curve identity kills it on every proper effective divisor H of dimension at most one, including empty or nonreduced H. On integral nonempty X, global generation yields two nonzero sections, which are regular and represent D as E-F. The shift identity allows arbitrary first argument C, so adding F1,F2 and cancelling proves additivity for arbitrary divisors. Symmetry and the integral Cartier/Picard isomorphism give both line-bundle identities. F7 alone was repaired; the Statement and actual AC assumption are unchanged. This is a local repair review, not an independent review of the repair.
